_readme: Copy this file to launcher.local.json (same folder) and edit it.
launcher.local.json is git-ignored on purpose: this repository is public, and
the only machine-specific fact Orrery needs is where your projects live.
Everything else about a project - its directory NAME, command, and port - is
portable and lives in the dev block in ../projects.json.
Every key below is optional. Delete the ones you do not need.
The two optional sections ship under _example_ names so that copying this
file verbatim changes nothing: rename the key to activate the section.
_projects_root: The folder that CONTAINS your project folders. Orrery joins each project's
dev.dir onto it, so with the value below it looks for the liminality project
Resolution order: the ORRERY_ROOT environment variable wins, then this key,
then the parent of this repository (which is right for the usual layout, so
most of the time you need no local file at all).
Forward slashes work fine on Windows; backslashes must be doubled in JSON.
Leave this pointing at a folder that does not exist and Orrery says so on
the board rather than pretending - but edit it, that is the point of the file.
_project_dirs: Escape hatch for a project that does not live under projects_root.
Keyed by project id (the id field in projects.json), the value is an
absolute path to that project's folder. Overrides dev.dir for that project.
Rename the key below to "project_dirs" to switch it on. A wrong path here
is reported on the card, not hidden - but an unedited example pointing at a
drive you do not have is still noise nobody asked for.
_disabled: Project ids to hide from this machine's launcher. They stay in projects.json
and on every other machine; they just do not appear as cards here.
Rename the key below to "disabled" to switch it on. Whatever is listed is
named in /api/health and on the board, so a hidden project is never a
_local_projects: Projects that exist only on this machine and must never appear in the
public repository: client work under NDA, anything where the folder name
and the run command are themselves the disclosure.
Each entry is shaped exactly like a projects.json entry - an id, a name,
an optional tagline and lanes, and a dev block - and once loaded it is
treated like any other project: start, stop, health, git status, the open
buttons and context all work the same. Cards are badged 'local'.
An id already in projects.json is skipped rather than overriding it, so a
git-ignored file can never silently contradict published data.
Rename the key below to "local_projects" to switch it on.
_open_commands: The "Open in" buttons - Code, Cursor, Claude, Folder - find their
executables on PATH with shutil.which, so on a normal install you need
nothing here. This is the escape hatch for a tool installed somewhere PATH
does not reach: the value is the command to run, either a bare name to look
up or a full path to the executable itself.
Keys: vscode, cursor, claude, folder, and "terminal" for the terminal the
claude button opens in (Windows Terminal, wt, by default; without it the
CLI opens in a plain console window instead).
Rename the key below to "open_commands" to switch it on. A target that
cannot be resolved answers 409 with the reason and its button is disabled
on the board - it never fails silently. Absolute paths belong HERE, in this
git-ignored file, and never in projects.json or orrery.py.
